facts.statement: Hadrosaurus lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous Period, approximately 83.6 to 77.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Hadrosaurus (; ) is a genus of hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaurs that lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous Period in what is now the Woodbury Formation in New Jersey about 83.6 to 77.9 million years ago.

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus were large animals that ranged from 7 to 8 meters in length and weighed between 2 and 4 tonnes.
facts.quote: They were large animals ranging from 7 to 8 m in length and 2 to 4 t in weight.

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus had a ponderous build, keratinous beaks for cropping foliage, and specialized complex teeth for processing food.
facts.quote: Hadrosaurus were ponderously built animals equipped with keratinous beaks for cropping foliage and a specialized and complex dentition for food processing.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Hadrosaurus was found in sediment where the animal's body was transported by a river and deposited in the sea.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen was found in fluvial marine sedimentation, meaning that the corpse of the animal was transported by a river and washed out to sea.

facts.statement: William Parker Foulke discovered the rest of the Hadrosaurus bones in 1858 after initially finding them in a marl pit.
facts.quote: In 1858, the bones sparked the interest of a visitor, William Parker Foulke, who dug out the rest of the bones from the marl pit in the same year.

facts.statement: Joseph Leidy formally described and named Hadrosaurus foulkii in 1858 to honor his collaborator William Parker Foulke.
facts.quote: in 1858, Leidy formally described and named Hadrosaurus foulkii in honor of his collaborator.

facts.statement: The name Hadrosaurus is derived from Greek words meaning "bulky" or "large" and "lizard".
facts.quote: The name Hadrosaurus was scientifically justified as deriving from the Greek ἁδρός, , meaning "bulky" or "large", and σαῦρος, , meaning "lizard".

facts.statement: Because the Hadrosaurus skeleton lacks a skull and was viewed as too incomplete, most scientists considered it a dubious name (nomen dubium) for a long time.
facts.quote: Despite the fact that the family Hadrosauridae has Hadrosaurus as its type genus, the skeleton lacks a skull and was long viewed as too incomplete to compare to other hadrosaurs for classification purposes, leading most scientists to consider it a nomen dubium, or dubious name.

facts.statement: A 2008 study found that Hadrosaurus was more primitive than lambeosaurines and classic hadrosaurines like Edmontosaurus and Saurolophus.
facts.quote: In a 2008 study, Hadrosaurus was found to be more primitive than either lambeosaurines or other "hadrosaurines", and not a particularly close relative of classic "hadrosaurines" such as Edmontosaurus and Saurolophus.

facts.statement: Studies using CT scans and fluoroscopy discovered evidence of various tumors, including hemangiomas and metastatic cancer, in Hadrosaurus vertebrae.
facts.quote: Evidence of tumors, including hemangiomas, desmoplastic fibroma, metastatic cancer and osteoblastoma were discovered in specimens of Hadrosaurus by analyzing dinosaur vertebrae using computerized tomography and fluoroscope screening.

facts.statement: Radiometric dating of bivalve shells from the formation where the holotype was found dates the rocks between 80.5 and 78.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Through the radiometric dating of bivalve shells known from the formation, the sedimentary rocks where the holotype specimen of Hadrosaurus was found have been dated from 80.5 million to 78.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: The genus Hadrosaurus was named by Joseph Leidy in 1858.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Leidy, 1858

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus fossils date to the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 80.5 to 78.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 80,5 a 78,5 millones de años, en el Campaniense

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus lived in what is now North America.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: In 1858, a Hadrosaurus skeleton became the first North American dinosaur known from more than isolated teeth.
facts.quote: En 1858, un esqueleto de un dinosaurio de este género fue el primer dinosaurio conocido por algo más que dientes aislados que se encontraron en Norteamérica

facts.statement: In 1868, the Hadrosaurus specimen became the first dinosaur skeleton ever mounted.
facts.quote: En 1868, se convirtió en el primer esqueleto montado de un dinosaurio

facts.statement: The discovery of Hadrosaurus began in 1838 in New Jersey when William Estaugh Hopkins found large bones.
facts.quote: El hallazgo tuvo lugar en 1838, en Nueva Jersey, cuando William Estaugh Hopkins encontró unos grandes huesos

facts.statement: William Parker Foulke saw the bones displayed in Hopkins' home and helped excavate the complete skeleton in 1858.
facts.quote: Posteriormente, los exhibió en su propia casa, en la misma localidad, y estos primeros huesos llamaron la atención de un visitante, William Parker Foulke, por lo que el esqueleto fue desenterrado completamente en 1858

facts.statement: Leidy's detailed monograph on Hadrosaurus was written in 1860 but published in 1865 due to the American Civil War.
facts.quote: La monografía de Leidy "Los reptiles cretáceos de los Estados Unidos", describiendo al Hadrosaurus más extensamente y con ilustraciones, fueron escritos en 1860 pero la Guerra Civil Norteamericana retrasó su publicación hasta 1865

facts.statement: The remains were mounted as the world's first dinosaur skeleton in 1868.
facts.quote: Los restos se convirtieron en 1868 en el primer esqueleto montado de dinosaurio del mundo

facts.statement: Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins was part of the team that fully mounted the skeleton in 1868.
facts.quote: El esqueleto entero fue montado totalmente en 1868 por un equipo que incluía al escultor y naturalista Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus was designated the state fossil of New Jersey in 1994.
facts.quote: Hadrosaurus fue nombrado el fósil del estado de Nueva Jersey , designado en 1994

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus was a bipedal dinosaur that used its front legs to support itself while feeding.
facts.quote: De andar bípedo, el Hadrosaurus podía utilizar sus patas delanteras para sostenerse al alimentarse

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus was a herbivore that likely ate leaves and clusters of vegetation.
facts.quote: Como todos los hadrosáuridos, era herbívoro, la conformación de sus dientes sugiere que se alimentaba de hojas y ramilletes

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus is estimated to have been about 8 meters long, 3 meters tall, and weighed 3 tons.
facts.quote: Se estima que midió unos 8 metros de longitud y entre 3 de altura, pesando 3 toneladas

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus had a duck-like beak used for pulling leaves from trees.
facts.quote: Tenía un pico similar al de los patos con el que arrancaba las hojas de los árboles

facts.statement: A 1922 stomach content analysis of a hadrosaurid revealed seeds and twigs.
facts.quote: En 1922 se analizó el contenido del estómago de un hadrosáurido y se hallaron semillas y ramas

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus had rows of tightly packed, serrated teeth at the back of its toothless, wide beak.
facts.quote: En el fondo de su pico ancho sin dientes, Hadrosaurus tenía varias hileras de dientes apretados formando una superficie rasposa

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus used its powerful jaws to cut and crush tough food with its irregular tooth edges.
facts.quote: Al mover arriba y abajo sus musculosas mandíbulas, los bordes irregulares de los dientes cortaban y trituraban los alimentos más duros

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus had a row of bony rods along its back supporting its spine.
facts.quote: A lo largo del dorso, Hadrosaurus tenía un espaldar de varillas óseas que sostenían su espinazo

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus had long spines on the underside of its tail to increase surface area.
facts.quote: En la parte inferior de la cola presentaba largas púas para aumentar su superficie

facts.statement: It is suggested that Hadrosaurus lived in groups.
facts.quote: Hadrosaurus tendría un comportamiento gregario

facts.statement: Leidy identified the bones as dinosaurian based on their similarity to Iguanodon, noting the Hadrosaurus specimen was more complete.
facts.quote: Leidy reconoció que los huesos eran de dinosaurio por su similitud con los de los de Iguanodon, descubierto en Inglaterra algunas décadas antes, aunque el de Hadrosaurus estaba más completo

facts.statement: While dinosaurs were thought to resemble rhinoceroses, Leidy reconstructed Hadrosaurus as bipedal because its front legs were much shorter than its hind legs.
facts.quote: En aquella época se creía que los dinosaurios se parecían a los rinocerontes, pero Leidy observó que el Hadrosaurus presentaba patas delanteras muchos más cortas que las traseras, por lo que lo reconstruyó como bípedo

facts.statement: Many scientists considered Hadrosaurus a nomen dubium because its skeleton lacks a skull and is too incomplete for comparison with other hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: A pesar de que la familia Hadrosauridae tiene a Hadrosaurus como su género tipo, el esqueleto carece de cráneo y es demasiado incompleto como para compararlo con otros hadrosaurinos para propósitos de clasificación, lo que llevó a muchos científicos a considerarlo como un nomen dubium.

facts.statement: A 2011 review by Prieto-Márquez concluded that Hadrosaurus possesses enough characteristics to ensure its validity.
facts.quote: En una revisión reciente de Prieto-Márquez del año (2011 indica que posee suficientes características para asegurar su validez.

facts.statement: In 2010, Prieto-Márquez defined the subfamily Hadrosaurinae as the lineage containing exclusively H. foulkii, renaming the previously named crestless subfamily Saurolophinae.
facts.quote: Asimismo anteriormente Prieto-Márquez en 2010 definió a Hadrosaurinae como el linaje que contenía exclusivamente a H. foulkii, mientras que la subfamilia de hadrosáuridos sin cresta habitualmente denominados de esa forma fue renombrada como Saurolophinae.

facts.statement: A 2008 study found that Hadrosaurus is more primitive than lambeosaurinids or other hadrosaurinids and is distantly related to classic hadrosaurines like Edmontosaurus or Saurolophus.
facts.quote: siguiendo la línea de un estudio de 2008, en el que se encontró que Hadrosaurus es más primitivo que los Lambeosaurinídos o los otros "hadrosaurinídos", y de hecho está distantemente relacionado con los "hadrosaurinos" clásicos como Edmontosaurus o Saurolophus.

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus is classified within the parent group Brachylophosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Brachylophosaurini

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus belongs to the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Hadrosaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
